children: Nomura continues to prefer Bajaj Finance, Tata Capital and L&T Finance among diversified NBFCs, and Shriram Finance among vehicle financiers, despite rising funding costs and increasing regulatory concerns.
The brokerage has a 'Buy' rating on Bajaj Finance, L&T Finance, Tata Capital and Shriram Finance. It also has a 'Buy' rating on Aadhar Housing Finance among housing financiers.

Nomura expects cost-of-fund pressure to result in 1-12% earnings-per-share cuts for its covered NBFCs over FY27F-28F, while its scenario analysis indicates a 1-8% hit to FY27F EPS if the RBI raises rates by 50-60 basis points.
"Structurally EPS compounding rate (FY27-29F CAGR) remains healthy at c.16-28%," Nomura said in a September 30 report.

Bond yields for AAA-rated and AA+ rated NBFCs have risen 29-70 basis points since the RBI's hawkish tilt in the Monetary Policy Committee minutes issued on August 19. Volatile global events have also prompted several NBFCs to stay away from the bond market.

The bond issuance run-rate of Bajaj Finance, L&T Finance and HDB Financial Services is behind the year-ago period in the first half of FY27. Nomura expects bond market activity to pick up in the second half of FY27, but at a higher cost. AAA-rated three-, five- and 10-year bond yields stood at 8.2-8.4% as of September 29, above the yields on bonds maturing over the next few quarters for its covered NBFCs.

Nomura had earlier expected NBFCs to benefit from relatively low-cost FCNR(B) flows raised by banks. However, it now expects banks to first use these flows to lower their own funding costs and then lend to low-risk segments such as mortgages and large corporates. As a result, only select NBFCs are expected to benefit in 2Q27F.

Nomura's economists expect two rate hikes totalling 50 basis points during October-December 2026. Its scenario assumes the entire 50-60 basis point increase takes effect in October, raising NBFC funding costs from 3Q27F, while lending rates are increased only from FY28F. Under this scenario, FY27F EPS could take a 1-8% hit, with the impact declining in FY28-29F as lending rates rise.

While Nomura believes the structural strengths of NBFCs remain intact in a rising-rate environment, it said recent regulatory developments are "more concerning". These include insurance distribution reforms affecting credit-life insurance policies offered by NBFCs and regulatory hesitation around flexi loans.
The brokerage said many diversified NBFCs have a healthy mix of floating-rate assets, while fixed-rate loans typically have shorter tenures, supporting profitability over FY27-29F.

title: Why Nomura remains positive on Bajaj Finance, Tata Capital, L&T Finance and Shriram Finance
